subject.title: fix(sqlite): stop mount probes blocking database startup

question: Should SQLite opening ever synchronously launch the system `mount` command, or must unavailable native classification immediately select rollback journaling without a subprocess?
rationale: The timeout improves the common stalled-process case but cannot establish a hard startup deadline under the documented synchronous child-process contract; retaining the probe therefore requires an explicit owner decision about the accepted availability and compatibility boundary.

options.title: Remove the startup subprocess
options.body: Use native or prepared classification only and conservatively select rollback journaling when those facts cannot classify the filesystem.

options.title: Accept the bounded-probe policy
options.body: Retain the synchronous probe only with explicit owner acceptance and supported-host proof covering slow classification, timeout, and journal-mode behavior.

recommendation.title: Remove the startup subprocess
recommendation.body: Use native or prepared classification only and conservatively select rollback journaling when those facts cannot classify the filesystem.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the current assignee and have carried the branch's successive SQLite startup-boundary refinements.
